claimBoundary: This experiment isolates the 8-bit YCbCr-to-RGB conversion arithmetic from entropy decoding, IDCT and chroma reconstruction. Pinned libjpeg-turbo first decodes each generated JPEG to full-resolution interleaved JCS_YCbCr with JDCT_ISLOW and do_fancy_upsampling=TRUE; ImageCraft receives only those full-resolution bytes.

The RGB reference is the same pinned libjpeg-turbo installation decoding the same JPEG with JDCT_ISLOW and its default fancy upsampling. The pinned jdmaster use_merged_upsample predicate rejects merged upsampling whenever do_fancy_upsampling is true, so the RGB reference and JCS_YCbCr probe both use the separate upsampling path; any remaining RGB difference is attributable to color conversion rather than a merged h2v1/h2v2 fast path.

The matrix crosses 4:4:4, 4:2:2, 4:4:0 and 4:2:0 with baseline/progressive coding, three qualities and three deterministic RGB source patterns. The encoded SOF sampling factors and coding mode are independently parsed before comparison.

ImageCraft output must match pinned libjpeg RGB byte-for-byte. No tolerance is introduced. Passing qualifies only the integer 8-bit YCbCr-to-RGB primitive on the observed full-resolution YCbCr domain; it does not by itself qualify JPEG entropy, IDCT, chroma upsampling, color management or a production color backend.
